name: Cheerio
prompt:
In this folder, set up a small Node.js project (ES modules) that uses Cheerio to scrape product data from HTML. Create `solution.mjs` that exports `parseProducts(html, pageUrl)`, which takes the HTML of a shop listing page (a string; do not fetch anything) and the URL that page was loaded from, and returns an array with one object per product, in page order:

`{ title, price, url, inStock }`

- Each product is an element with the class `product`. Ignore everything else on the page.
- `title`: the text of the product's `.product-title` element, trimmed, with runs of whitespace collapsed to a single space and HTML entities decoded.
- `price`: the current price from the product's `.price` element as a number in dollars (for example `"$1,299.00"` becomes `1299`). Some products show a crossed-out old price inside a `<del>` element in `.price`; ignore it.
- `url`: the `href` of the product's `a.product-link`, turned into an absolute URL resolved against `pageUrl` (relative links like `chair` or `../sale/rug` must be resolved the way a browser would).
- `inStock`: `false` if the product element also has the class `sold-out`, otherwise `true`.

Install the dependencies with npm.
